system.name: Relay
system.description: Carries delivery scans from couriers' handhelds to the depot routing records, the finance ledger and the recipient's phone

people.name: Courier
people.description: Scans a parcel on a handheld; the handheld posts the scan to the intake API

people.name: Recipient
people.description: Waits for the parcel and gets a text saying which depot it is on its way to

people.name: Finance team
people.description: Owns and runs the ledger Relay writes to, and bills the depots from it

containers.name: Intake API
containers.description: Accepts a parcel scan on POST /scans, decodes it and publishes it to the bus as delivery.scanned; it keeps no state of its own

containers.name: Router
containers.description: Consumes delivery.scanned, picks the depot from the reference prefix, records the route, appends a charge to the finance ledger and publishes delivery.routed

containers.name: Notifier
containers.description: Consumes delivery.routed and texts the recipient through the SMS provider; it never calls the router back

containers.name: Message bus
containers.description: Carries delivery.scanned and delivery.routed; it is the only path between the three services, which never call each other

containers.name: Routes database
containers.description: One row per routed parcel: its reference and the depot it was sent to, keyed by the generated route id

containers.name: Finance ledger
containers.technology: PostgreSQL, run by the finance platform
containers.description: The finance platform's billing ledger on ledger.finance.example; Relay only ever appends charge rows and does not own the schema

external_systems.name: SMS provider
external_systems.description: HTTP gateway that delivers the 'parcel on its way' text to the recipient's phone

excluded.reason: Local development convenience only: an inbox that catches the texts the notifier would have sent, so the team does not pay for them. It is never deployed (docker-compose.yml:41, README.md:32-34) and no Relay code talks to it.

summary.overview: Relay moves delivery scans from the handhelds couriers carry to the people and systems that need to know about them. A courier's handheld posts a scan to the Go intake API, which validates it and publishes delivery.scanned to a RabbitMQ bus; the Python router consumes that, derives the depot from the parcel reference, writes the route to its own PostgreSQL database, appends a charge row to a ledger the finance platform owns, and publishes delivery.routed; the Node notifier consumes that and texts the recipient through an external SMS provider. No service calls another directly - the topic names in contracts/ are the entire contract between them - and the only database Relay owns is the routes one. A Mailpit inbox and a json-server SMS stub exist for local development and are not deployed.
findings: The router does four separate side effects per message with no transaction and acks only at the end (`router/router/main.py:10-21`): the route row, the ledger charge, the published message and the ack. A crash or redelivery after the route insert re-runs all of them, so one scan can produce two route rows and bill the depot twice; a crash after the insert and before the publish leaves a parcel routed, billed and never announced.

Nothing makes the handling idempotent: `record` always inserts a new row (`router/router/routes.py:15-18`) and `append` always inserts a new charge (`router/router/ledger.py:16-19`), and neither uses the parcel reference as a key, so AMQP's at-least-once delivery turns directly into duplicate billing.

Relay writes straight into a database another team owns, over a connection string pointing at their host (`router/router/ledger.py:15`, `docker-compose.yml:28`). The coupling is at the schema level with no API in between, and the README says nobody here may change that schema (`README.md:27-28`).

The notifier's consumer callback awaits `sendText` without a try/catch (`notifier/src/index.ts:12-17`); when the SMS provider answers 4xx or 5xx, `sendText` throws (`notifier/src/sms.ts:11-13`), the message is never acked and the rejection is unhandled. There is no retry, dead-letter queue or alert on that path.

The shared contract is only shared with one of the three services: `contracts/src/index.ts:1-2` is TypeScript, so the Go publisher re-declares the topic name (`intake/internal/bus/publisher.go:11`) and the Python router re-declares both (`router/router/bus.py:7-8`). A rename in contracts/ would silently break two of the three services.
The price of a routed parcel is a constant in the consumer (`router/router/main.py:6`, CHARGE_CENTS = 180), so changing what a depot is billed means shipping the router.

Every message opens and closes two PostgreSQL connections (`router/router/routes.py:14`, `router/router/ledger.py:15`) - one per store, per scan - with no pooling, and the router consumes one message at a time (`router/router/main.py:19`).
Bus, routes and ledger credentials are literals in the compose file (`docker-compose.yml:10-12`, `docker-compose.yml:26-28`), including the one for the finance platform's host.

The intake API's `/healthz` reports the process, not the dependency it cannot work without (`intake/cmd/intake/main.go:23`): it answers 200 while the bus connection opened at start-up (`intake/cmd/intake/main.go:15`) is down and every POST /scans is returning 502.
recommendations: Make the router's handling idempotent before anything else: a unique constraint on the parcel reference in both `routes` and `ledger_entries`, with inserts that do nothing on conflict, so a redelivered delivery.scanned cannot double-bill a depot.
Write the route row and the outgoing delivery.routed message in one transaction (an outbox table drained by the publisher), so a parcel can never be recorded and billed without being announced.

Replace the direct write into the finance platform's ledger with an interface finance owns - an append endpoint or a topic they consume - so their schema is no longer a build-time dependency of Relay.
Wrap the notifier's `sendText` call in a try/catch that nacks the message to a dead-letter queue instead of leaving it unacked, and alert on that queue.
Generate or publish the topic names for Go and Python from `contracts/` instead of retyping them, so the three services cannot drift apart.
Move the charge per parcel out of the router's source into configuration, and move the compose credentials - the finance one above all - into secrets.
